item.title: Joining a project
item.description:
A project belongs to whoever created it. To get onto somebody else’s project you ask for a place on it with a short code, and one of that project’s owners decides. Nobody joins by holding the code alone.

You need a connection for this part

Joining is the one thing in TriTrack that cannot be done in the field. Everything else — recording bearings, reading the map, working through a whole day out of signal — works with no connection at all. Asking to join, and the approval coming back, both need the phone to reach the server.

item.title: Projects, members and roles
item.description:
Everything TriTrack records belongs to a project: the tags, the bearings, the position estimates, the map extent. One device can hold several, and one of them is active at a time — the one with the green tick in the list.

Tap a project’s name to make it the active one. Everything else is behind the three-dot button at the end of the row, with each entry written out: Publish to server , Members , Edit project , Leave project and, last and separated from the rest, Delete project .

item.title: Recording a bearing
item.description:
This is the thing you will do a hundred times a day. Pick the animal, point the antenna, capture the direction, save.

These two screenshots are of a device with no project server set up, which is why there is no coloured bar across the top. Once a device is syncing there is one; the sync page explains what it says.

item.title: Comparing bearings on the map
item.description:
Two bearings taken from the same spot tell you very little. Two taken from widely separated spots cross somewhere, and that crossing is the animal. The problem is that the map draws every bearing at the same modest length, so the rays you want to compare stop short of each other and you end up extending them in your head.

Since September 2026 you can extend them on the screen instead.

item.title: Truth points
item.description:
A truth point is the record of a place somebody physically went to and found the animal, the collar, or both. It is the only record in TriTrack that says where something actually was rather than where the radio suggested it was.

That is what makes it worth the two minutes it takes. Everything else the app produces is an inference from bearings; a truth point is the thing you check those inferences against — how far out was the estimate, and was it out in a way that says something about the terrain, the antenna or the observer.

item.title: Sync
item.description:
TriTrack records everything on the device first. Sync is what gets it to the server and to your teammates, and gets theirs to you. Nothing you do in the field waits for it.

TriTrack works with no server at all

If you never set up a server connection, the app is complete: projects, tags, bearings, position estimates, the map, exports. There is no bar across the top, nothing tries to reach the network, and nothing nags you about it. A one-person season on one phone is a supported way to use this app, not a degraded one.

item.title: Getting your data out
item.description:
Two ways out, for two different jobs. A spreadsheet is for analysis. A backup file is for moving a whole project, or for making sure a phone is not the only place your season exists.

Open More , then Data Export / Backup .

item.title: Privacy policy
item.description:
This policy has not been written yet.

The page exists because the URL has to exist and because a visible gap is honest where a missing page is not. It will say what TriTrack stores on the device, what leaves the device when a project is synced to a server, who can read it, and how long any of it is kept.

Until it is written, treat nothing on this page as a commitment. If you need an answer before then, see Support.

item.title: Support
item.description:
This page is mostly not written yet. It will carry the ways to report a problem or ask a question, and what the app is and is not expected to do without a network connection. One part of it is written, because it is the part that makes every report usable.

Which version are you on?

Open More and choose App Info . The first line is the version and the build number, and it is selectable — long-press to copy it and paste it into your report.
